contexts.evidence: Theorem 2.1 and its proof (p. 3) identify finite ReLU networks with continuous piecewise-linear functions and prove depth at most ceil(log2(d+1))+1; the CPWL claim relevant to this citation is supported.

Theorem 2.1 (p. 3) proves the dimension-dependent bound, but the same page explicitly credits Goodfellow et al. (2013), Proposition 4.1, with an earlier version without a depth bound. Attributing the equivalence itself solely to Arora et al. overstates priority.
contexts.proposed_replacement: The converse also holds: \emph{every} \ac{cpwl} function is exactly representable by a \ac{relu} network of bounded depth. The dimension-dependent depth bound of \textcite{Arora2018} is the entry point for the difference-of-convex analysis of Chapter~\ref{ch:decompositions}.

contexts.evidence: Theorem 2.1 (p. 3) is exactly the stated equivalence and depth bound. Definition 1 (p. 2) counts hidden layers plus the final output transformation, matching the displayed +1.

Theorem 2.1 proof, Eq. (2.1), p. 3, uses signed maxima of at most d+1 affine functions, explicitly attributed to Wang and Sun (2005), Theorem 1. The final tree count should be called hidden-layer count: with the paper and thesis depth convention the affine output contributes +1.
contexts.proposed_replacement: The stated depth bound, which is uniform in the number of affine pieces and depends only on the input dimension $d$, follows from \textcite{Arora2018}, who use the Wang--Sun representation of every \ac{cpwl} function on $\RR^d$ as a signed sum of maxima of at most $d+1$ affine functions each. These maxima require at most $\lceil\log_2(d+1)\rceil$ hidden layers, followed by a final affine output layer.

contexts.evidence: Section 2.2, Proposition 4 (paper p. 4), and Appendix B.2 (supplement PDF pp. 13–14), recursively represent ReLU networks as DC functions.
